title: Agentic Runtime Security — Bedrock AgentCore + HashiCorp Vault
footer: Step-through of the AgentCore + Vault request path. Vault never authenticates the user — it validates an AgentCore-issued JWT via JWKS, and that seam is the only trust boundary between the two systems.

overview.title: Full architecture — 7-step request path
overview.html: End user → AgentCore Runtime → AgentCore Identity → JWKS seam → Vault → JIT credentials → protected resources → audit → answer. Press Play, or click any numbered chip to jump straight to that step.

complete.title: Complete — one trust plane each, one seam between them
complete.html: AgentCore owns identity and runtime; Vault owns authorization, credentials, and audit. They meet at exactly one place: Vault validating an AgentCore-issued JWT via JWKS. Vault never authenticates the user, and no credential outlives its lease.

steps.title: Authenticate + invoke
steps.html: The end user signs in against the external OIDC IdP (Cognito, Okta, Entra ID, IBM Verify — pluggable) using OAuth 2.0 + PKCE, then invokes the agent. AgentCore Runtime is managed and serverless: no EKS, no ServiceAccounts, no NetworkPolicy to operate.

steps.title: Issue user-context JWT
steps.html: The runtime asks AgentCore Identity for a token. The JWT carries both the agent's workload identity (ARN) and the end user's identity claims. The Secure Token Vault holds short-lived user-delegated OAuth tokens (on-behalf-of) — this replaces IVIA / CIBA out-of-band consent.

steps.title: Present JWT → Vault validates (the seam)
steps.html: Vault's OAuth resource server validates the signature against AgentCore's JWKS endpoint — no separate Vault login step. The Agent Registry checks the agent is a registered identity entity with approved scopes (unregistered agents are blocked), and authorization is bound to the authorization_details claim in the JWT body. This JWKS trust is the only seam between the two systems.

steps.title: Vend short-lived JIT credentials
steps.html: The dynamic secrets engine mints per-request credentials — DB (Postgres, MySQL, Mongo), AWS IAM, SSH, PKI, KV — scoped to that authorization and TTL-bound to the JWT lease. No standing privileges: the credentials die when the lease expires.

steps.title: Access protected resources
steps.html: The agent reaches databases, AWS IAM/STS and SaaS APIs, SSH/PKI/KV, and Bedrock Nova models only with the Vault-vended, short-lived credentials. Everything auto-revokes at lease expiry — no rotation scripts.

steps.title: Every credential request is logged
steps.html: Vault writes each request to its hash-chained, tamper-evident audit log: agent identity, resolved user identity from the JWT claims, JWT metadata, credential lease ID, timestamp. One audit stream answers who caused which query — replacing the old 3-plane Athena JOIN across IVIA, Vault, and pgaudit.

steps.title: Stream the answer back
steps.html: The result streams back to the user. User attribution is preserved end-to-end on every hop — and because each credential was leased, not granted, the agent holds nothing once the task ends.
